configurator.airTitle: How much air are we supplying?
configurator.airHint: Enter the airflow per diffuser. If you don’t know it, calculate it from the room size.
configurator.airflowHint: How much air passes through one diffuser per hour. Taken from the ventilation design or from the air change rate.
configurator.distanceHint: Distance from the diffuser to where people are (usually ceiling height minus 1.8 m). The closer it is, the higher the air velocity near people.
configurator.deltaTHint: Difference between room and supply air temperature (e.g. the air conditioner supplies air 8 K colder). Default is 10 K, as in the manufacturer’s selection program; 0 — don’t calculate.
configurator.roomShow: Don’t know the airflow? Calculate it from the room
configurator.roomChangesHint: How many times per hour the air is renewed: homes 1–2, offices 2–4, kitchens/bathrooms 5–10.
configurator.sizeHint: Nominal size — to fit the opening or the duct. We mark the smallest size that works quietly and without draughts.
configurator.planksNote: The number after “/” is the number of adjustable slats.
configurator.lengthHint: Total length of the diffuser. Long runs are assembled from several sections.
configurator.slotAdvice: For {airflow} m³/h with the selected number of slots we recommend a length of at least {length} mm.
configurator.unavailable: Not available for the selected size
configurator.colorHint: The body is powder coated. Standard is white RAL 9016; other colours are made to order.
configurator.calcHint: Approximate calculation based on reference coefficients. For critical projects the final selection is checked by an engineer.
configurator.freeAreaHint: The area air actually passes through (excluding frame and blades).
configurator.velocityHint: Up to {good} m/s — quiet (homes, offices), up to {ok} m/s — acceptable, above that — audible noise.
configurator.zoneHint: Air velocity near people. Up to {good} m/s — comfortable, above {ok} m/s — draughts are felt.
configurator.pressureHint: How much pressure the diffuser “eats”. Up to {good} Pa — good, over {ok} Pa — the fan will work harder and louder.
configurator.deltaTZone: Temperature difference in the occupied zone ≈ {value} K
configurator.deltaTBad: — noticeable; better increase the size or the distance.
configurator.calcDisabled: For this model the selection is made by an engineer using the manufacturer’s charts — add it to your request and we’ll send you the calculation.
configurator.calcNeedAirflow: Enter the airflow to see the calculation.
configurator.calcBadDims: Check the dimensions — they are outside the allowed range.
configurator.tipVelocity: Outlet velocity is too high — it will be noisy. Choose a larger size or use several diffusers.
configurator.tipZone: There will be a draught near people. Increase the size or the number of diffusers, or choose a swirl type.
configurator.tipPressure: High resistance: the fan will need more pressure. Increase the size.
configurator.verdictGood: ✓ This size fits: quiet, no draughts and low resistance.
configurator.verdictOk: It will work, but with little margin — for living rooms a larger size is better.
configurator.vizThrow: The jet slows to {v} m/s within {l} m

guide.title: How to choose a diffuser
guide.s1Text: It is usually given in the ventilation design. If not: area × height × air change rate. Air changes: homes 1–2, offices 2–4, kitchens and bathrooms 5–10. Divide the total airflow by the number of diffusers in the room.
guide.s2Title: 2. Choose the type for your ceiling and interior
types: Apartments, offices and shops with ceilings up to 3.5 m. Distribute air in 1–4 directions along the ceiling.
Swirl and panel diffusers (DPF, RD, DCc)
Armstrong grid ceilings, offices, open spaces. The swirling jet mixes air quickly — fewer draughts at high airflow.
Modern interiors, stretch and plasterboard ceilings. A linear jet along the ceiling or a window. SDH — concealed, plastered-in installation.
Almost invisible: built into the ceiling and painted together with it. For small airflows in living rooms.
Swirl diffusers and nozzles (VDL, DVA, JN)
High rooms of 4–15 m: warehouses, halls, shopping centres. Swirl diffusers with a thermostatic element switch between heating and cooling automatically; JN nozzles throw air 10–30 m.
guide.s3Title: 3. Check three numbers in the configurator
guide.s3Velocity: Outlet velocity — up to {good} m/s for quiet rooms, up to {ok} m/s for commercial spaces.
guide.s3Zone: Velocity in the occupied zone — up to {good} m/s to avoid draughts.
guide.s3Pressure: Pressure drop — preferably up to {good} Pa.
guide.s3Note: The configurator highlights them in green, yellow or red and recommends a size itself.
guide.s4Text: The standard colour is white RAL 9016. Any other RAL colour is painted to order. Add items to your request — our manager will confirm the price and lead time.
